How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe and PayPal explicitly exclude a large number of countries from their services, forcing creators in those regions to either find workarounds or abandon their businesses altogether. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure is inherently inclusive, allowing creators from any country to utilize available tools for payment processing and product delivery. Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Payment speed and fees are critical factors for creators. Stripe and PayPal often impose high transaction fees and delays in fund availability, which can disrupt cash flow. Sovereign commerce infrastructure, on the other hand, offers rapid payment processing through platforms like NOWPayments, with only a 0.5% fee and no KYC requirements. This means creators can quickly access their funds and reinvest in their businesses, enhancing their operational agility.

Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Ownership of customer data and product delivery systems is a significant advantage of sovereign commerce infrastructure. With platforms like Stripe and PayPal, creators risk losing access to their customers if their accounts are banned or suspended. By using a decentralized infrastructure, creators maintain full control over their online stores. Automated payment processing, instant product delivery, and robust data management systems ensure that creators can focus on their craft rather than on administrative hurdles.
